transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

...My family made me come. I just... I keep telling them I'm the reason my friend died. I didn't call her back, and... I had ugly thoughts sometimes. Now I know the Lord is punishing everybody at the church because of me. I don't really want to talk about it, but that's why they brought me here.
Have you been hearing voices or sounds that other people don't seem to hear?
No. I don't... I haven't heard anything like that. Just my own thoughts.
Do you believe things that other people might find unusual or hard to understand, like thoughts that you know aren’t true but you can’t stop believing them?

I don't... I know they are true. It's just that other people don't understand. 

Like... at church. I don't really like talking about this. But when the pastor says the prayers, or... or when the choir sings certain lines... I know what they're doing. They're warning me. They know God has marked me, and that the church is suffering because I brought this on us. 

I don't really want to say any more about it.
Do you believe that things happening around you are related to you in a special or unusual way, even if others don’t see it that way?

I... I just told you about the church. I don't really know what else you mean. 

I mostly just stay home now anyway, so... no. Just what I already said. I don't want to keep going over it.
Do you feel like things happening in the world, like on TV or in the news, are secretly about you or meant as messages for you?
No. I don't... I don't really turn the television on much these days anyway. So... no. Nothing like that.
Do you feel that certain religious texts, prayers, or spiritual events are specifically directed at you or meant only for you to understand?

I... I thought we just went over this. 

I already told you about the church. When the pastor prays, or the choir sings those lines... they're warning me. They know God marked me. That it's my fault the church is suffering. 

I don't... I really don't want to keep talking about it. I already said it.
Do you ever feel that you have a special role or importance that others don’t recognize, like you were chosen for a unique purpose or have special abilities?
No. I don't... I don't have any special abilities. I'm just an old woman. There's nothing special about me. I don't really know why you'd ask me that.
Do you feel that certain events, actions, or words spoken by others—like during church services—are directed at you in a personal and meaningful way, even if others don’t see it that way?
I... I thought we just talked about the church. I told you what they say. I don't... I don't really have anything else to add to that. I don't know what else you want me to say.
Outside of your experience at church, do you feel like everyday events, like things people say or do, are directed at you in a special way?
No, not really. Just the church. I don't really notice anything else.
Do you believe, even deep down, that what you’re experiencing is actually real and happening to you—like the church really is suffering because of you?

I... yes. I know it is. 

When the pastor says the prayers... or when the choir sings certain lines... I just know they're warning me. God has marked me. The church is suffering because I brought this on us. It's not... it's just what's happening.
Outside of your thoughts about the church and your friend’s death, do you ever have unusual beliefs or suspicions about other things in your daily life that other people don’t seem to share?
No... I don't think so. I just... I go to work at the store and I come home. I don't really pay attention to much else. There's nothing else.
Do you ever feel responsible for events that happen to other people, even if you weren’t directly involved, like something bad happening to someone close to you was your fault?

I... well, yes. I've told them. My friend... she died because of me. I didn't call her back when I should have. And... sometimes I had ugly thoughts about her. It's my fault. That's why the Lord is punishing everyone at the church. Because of what I did.
Do your thoughts ever become so disorganized that you have trouble putting them together in a logical way, or do you ever find it hard to follow conversations or make yourself understood?
I... no. I don't think so. I can understand people fine. I just... I don't talk much anymore. But I know what they're saying. My thoughts are just... heavy. But they make sense.
Do these thoughts about being punished and the church suffering ever feel connected to how you're feeling emotionally, like they match the way you're feeling inside?

I... I suppose so. Yes. Before she died... before I got like this, I didn't think the pastor or the choir were... sending messages about me. That only started recently. After I got so low... and felt so guilty these past few weeks. It just feels like... like it all fits together now.
Do the thoughts you have about the church and your friend’s death make sense to you based on how you’ve been feeling emotionally, like they fit with how low or guilty you’ve been feeling?

I... yes, like I just said. Before she passed, before I sank into all this... I never believed the pastor or the choir were sending warnings about me. I didn't think that way. It only started these past few weeks... after I got so low. And the guilt... it just started then.
Do the thoughts you have about the church and being punished ever feel completely separate from how you’re feeling emotionally, like they don’t match your mood at all?

I... no, they don't feel separate. Like I was trying to explain... I didn't have these thoughts before she died. I never thought the choir or the pastor were... warning me about anything. That all started after I got so low. The guilt... the thoughts... they all came together these past few weeks. It's just... heavy.

inference_history.note: Initial presentation includes themes of guilt, rumination, and possible delusional thinking (e.g., belief that the Lord is punishing others because of the patient). This could indicate a major depressive episode with psychotic features, a primary psychotic disorder (e.g., schizophrenia, delusional disorder), or other psychotic disorders. Further questioning is needed to clarify the presence and duration of key symptoms such as hallucinations, delusions, mood disturbance, and to rule out other conditions.
